terms.meaning: The era believed to begin with Chandragupta I's reign in 320 C.E.
Harisena's Sanskrit praise of Samudragupta, carved on Ashoka's pillar.
The title earned by Chandragupta II.
The officials who made up the Gupta bureaucracy.
An ancient Buddhist university, supported by the Guptas and Harsha.

items.name: Chandragupta I
items.formula: Married a Licchavi princess and was called Maharajadhiraja.
items.example: Srigupta founded the dynasty, which rose in the 4th century C.E.

items.name: Samudragupta
items.formula: Ruled most of India and performed the Aswamedha yaga.
items.example: A poet and musician too: his gold coins show him playing the veena.

items.name: Chandragupta II
items.formula: Defeated the Sakas and added Western India.
items.example: His reign is remembered for literature and art more than battles.

items.name: Iron Pillar at Mehrauli
items.formula: 23 feet 8 inches tall, about 6,000 kg, and still not rusted.
items.example: It shows the metal skill of the time.

items.name: Why the Gupta Empire declined
items.formula: Hun attacks, powerful vassals, no large army of its own, and collapse of trade.
items.example: Pataliputra shrank to the size of a village.

items.name: Kalidasa's works
items.formula: Poems: Meghadoota, Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava, Ritu Samhara. Play: Abhijnana Shakuntala.
items.example: In Meghadoota, an exiled Yaksha sends a cloud with a message to his wife.

items.name: Other Gupta-age works
items.example: Puranas and Dharmashastras were also written then.

items.name: Story of Abhijnana Shakuntala
items.formula: Durvasa's curse makes Dushyanta forget Shakuntala; a ring found in a fish restores his memory.

items.name: Gupta-age medicine
items.formula: Dhanwantari: father of Indian medicine. Charaka: Charaka Samhita. Sushruta: surgery, Sushruta Samhita.
items.example: Sushruta mentions a separate wing to treat soldiers.

items.name: Aryabhata
items.formula: Astronomer and mathematician, believed to have invented zero.
items.example: He explained eclipses: solar when the Moon is between Sun and Earth, lunar when the Earth is between.

items.name: Varahamihira
items.example: Also Bruhat Samhita, Bruhat Jataka and Laghu Jataka.

items.name: Founder and kings of the Vardhanas
items.formula: Founder Pushyabhuti; famous kings Prabhakaravardhana and Harshavardhana.
items.example: They ruled from Thaneswar in the 6th century.

items.name: Harsha's conquests
items.formula: He beat Shashanka of Bengal, took Kanauj, and ruled Bengal and Magadha.
items.example: Pulikeshi II stopped him at the Narmada, as Ravikirti's Aihole inscription records.

items.name: Harsha's officials
items.example: Land tax was the main income.

items.name: Sources for Harsha's time
items.formula: Bana's Harshacharita and Hiuen Tsang's writings.

items.name: Facts about Nalanda
items.formula: Harsha gifted a 25 metre bronze Buddha.
items.example: Nagarjuna and Dharmapala taught there; Hiuen Tsang stayed there.

mistakes.text: Chandragupta I began the Gupta era; Chandragupta II was Vikramaditya. Both differ from Chandragupta Maurya.
Mudrarakshasa is by Vishakhadatta, not Kalidasa.
Harsha lost to Pulikeshi II at the Narmada; Pulikeshi was the winner.
